question: During profitable H4 long trades, which ranges of the signal candle's arithmetic features differ from losing ones, and does a range picked on older history still beat 'long every candle' on newer history?
population: every complete H4 candle on data/mt5/XAUUSD_M15.csv (2024-05-22..2026-05-21), LONG, same entry/stop/1.5R target/costs/funding as declaration.json
procedure: Train only: cut each feature into 5 equal-count bins (hour: its 5 to 6 actual values).
For each feature, the 'profit range' is the single contiguous run of 1-3 bins with the highest mean net R, holding at least 20% of train candidates.
Selection-noise check: repeat the same search 200 times with net R shuffled across candidates; a range counts only if its train gain over all-candles beats 95% of the shuffles.
Ranges that pass are frozen, then measured once on test: mean net R inside the range vs all test candles (the control).
pass_bar: a frozen range passes on test if its mean net R beats the test control by more than one standard error and is above 0, with at least 30 test candidates
caveats: This history was already used to look at this rule's aggregate results today (not per feature range).
Gold rose about 87% over the full history; the control removes the drift that all longs share.
